{{Short description|Nineteenth century mathematician}}'''Yitzchak ben Nechemia Ratner''' ({{langx|he|יצחק בן נחמיה ראטנער}}; 1857, [[Shklow|Shklov]], [[Russian Empire]] — ?) was a nineteenth-century [[Jew]]ish [[maskilic]] mathematician.<ref name=JE>{{Cite Jewish Encyclopedia|title=Ratner, Isaac|url=http://www.jewishencyclopedia.com/articles/12594-ratner-isaac|first1=Herman|last1=Rosenthal|first2=Isidor|last2=Warsaw}}</ref> He wrote mathematical and astronomical articles for various journals, and was the author of ''Mishpat Emet'' (1884), a criticism of [[Gabriel Judah Lichtenfeld|Lichtenfeld]]'s pamphlets against [[Hayyim Selig Slonimski|Slonimski]]'s works.<ref>{{cite book|title=Mishpat Emet|first=Isaac|last=Ratner|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XtMQAAAAYAAJ|year=1883|oclc=19152927}}</ref> In 1898 he edited a second edition of Slonimski's ''Yesodei Chokmat ha-Shi'ur'' on the principles of algebra.
